scams.name: Maya Bay National Park Fee Double-Billing
scams.description: You pay 1,800 baht for a speedboat day tour to Maya Bay from Ao Nang. At the Maya Bay entry point, the operator demands an additional 400 baht ‘national park entrance fee.’ The legitimate Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Koh Phi Phi National Park foreigner fee is 400 baht — but scam operators pocket it and don’t remit it to the park, charging tourists twice when the fee was already bundled into the tour price. r/ThailandTourism ‘So what’s the deal with the Maya Bay (Ko Phi Phi) entrance’ captures the confusion: other Thai national parks have proper ticket offices you pay directly; the Phi Phi tours obscure whether the fee was already included.
scams.avoidance: Book Maya Bay tours on Klook or 12go.asia with ‘park fee included’ explicit in the listing. Bring 400 baht per person in cash as a backup; if the tour says the fee is included, you still have protection against re-billing. For Phi Phi ferries, book directly with Chao Koh Ferry (chaokohferryphiphi.com) or Songserm — not booth middlemen. Confirm your ferry ticket destination in writing: ‘Phi Phi to Ao Nang’ and ‘Phi Phi to Krabi Town’ are different piers with different fees. Keep printed vouchers on you; operators occasionally try to double-bill even on prepaid tours.
scams.location: Maya Bay (on Phi Phi Leh), tour operator pickups from Phi Phi Don and Ao Nang

scams.name: Phi Phi ‘Bucket’ Drink Spiking & Watered Cocktails
scams.description: It’s party night on Loh Dalum Beach and a beach bar sells 300-baht ‘rum and coke’ buckets — a plastic sandcastle bucket filled with spirits, Red Bull, and mixer. You drink two and wake up in your hostel with no memory of the last three or four hours and 8,000 baht missing. r/travel ‘I fell for a tourist scam and feel really stupid’ documents the pattern: ‘I walked into the bar and immediately knew I’d walked into a scam. I was drunk (rum and pineapple served in a bucket) at Phi Phi.’ The Phi Phi bucket is a known vehicle for drink-spiking — spirits are mixed out of sight, benzodiazepines and GHB dissolve quickly in sugary cocktails, and the small plastic cups inside the bucket make it impossible to track individual drinks.
scams.avoidance: Don’t accept a bucket cocktail on Phi Phi. Order bottled beer or a cocktail mixed in front of you. Watch your drink being made and keep it in your hand; discard any drink you set down. Travel in groups — Phi Phi is walk-only and solo rescue options are limited. Store your passport, extra cards, and most cash at your accommodation; carry 1,000–2,000 baht and one card. If you feel suddenly drunk beyond your drink count, head to the hotel immediately and alert the night staff.
scams.location: Tonsai Village bars, Loh Dalum Beach parties, Sunflower Bar, Slinky Bar

scams.name: Phi Phi Ferry Middleman Ticket Markup
scams.description: You walk to a beachfront ferry booth in Ao Nang and buy a Phi Phi return for 1,400 baht. At the pier, you see tourists boarding the same ferry with tickets from Chao Koh Ferry or Songserm for 800. The booth you used was a middleman reseller, not the ferry company. r/ThailandTourism ‘Don’t use SiamFerry.com’ notes: ‘It’s not a scam — they’re a travel agent providing a service at a commission. No different from the thousand other travel-agent kiosks on the strip.’ Technically legal, but a 50–75 percent markup on publicly-priced ferry tickets.
scams.avoidance: Book Phi Phi ferries directly with Chao Koh Ferry (chaokohferryphiphi.com), Songserm, or Phi Phi Cruiser on their official sites. Specify the destination precisely in writing: ‘Ao Nang beach pier,’ not just ‘Krabi.’ During the monsoon (May–October), take the larger ferry over speedboats, and check Windy for wave conditions before boarding. Pay by credit card where possible; chargebacks resolve fly-by-night booking disputes. Keep the printed voucher and compare it to the actual ferry company’s schedule on arrival.
scams.location: Ao Nang beach pier, Rassada Pier (Phuket), Krabi Town Klong Chilad pier, Phi Phi Tonsai pier

scams.name: Tonsai Village Luggage Porter Overcharge
scams.description: You arrive at Phi Phi’s Tonsai Pier. A porter with a cart offers to carry your luggage to your hotel — ‘100 baht,’ you think you hear. At the hotel he demands 500 baht per bag. r/ThailandTourism ‘My first solo trip is a disaster’ captures the arrival chaos. Phi Phi is walk-only (no cars, no tuk-tuks), which makes porters genuinely useful — but the pricing is opaque and tourist-padded. The standard rate is 50–100 baht per bag for a short hotel transfer; 300+ baht per bag is aggressive upcharging.
scams.avoidance: Agree on price in writing on your phone before handing over any bags: ‘100 baht per bag, two bags, 200 baht total.’ Know the benchmarks: 50–100 baht per bag for a short porter transfer; 200–300 baht per group for Tonsai to Long Beach by longtail; 2,500–3,500 baht total for a full-day private longtail. Most Tonsai hotels are a 5–15 minute walk from the pier — you may not need a porter at all. Pay on arrival, not before; this maintains negotiation leverage. Photograph the porter’s tag or boat license number so you have accountability.
scams.location: Phi Phi Tonsai Pier, Tonsai Village walking paths, Long Beach trail

scams.name: Phi Phi Accommodation Over-Booking & ‘Upgrade’ Fee
scams.description: You arrive at your Phi Phi hostel with a printed Booking.com confirmation. The clerk says: ‘Sorry, we overbooked, but we have a better room in our other property for 500 baht extra per night.’ The ‘other property’ is a different bungalow with a worse bed and no Booking.com paper trail. r/ThailandTourism ‘I paid for a room on Agoda. When I arrived the staff told me…’ documents the Agoda variant: ‘Had the same in Phuket in November. Contacted Agoda and once they had clarified it with the hotel, they gave me a full refund within a week.’ The scam depends on you accepting the ‘upgrade’ on the spot without contacting the platform.
scams.avoidance: Book through Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb with credit-card payment and screenshot your confirmation. If overbooked on arrival, contact platform support immediately via in-app chat — don’t accept the ‘upgrade’ on the spot. Document every communication and the actual unit condition with photos and video. If forced to accept the alternative, dispute via the platform plus a credit-card chargeback on return. For Phi Phi peak season (December–February), book four weeks ahead and use free-cancellation windows as a backup.
scams.location: Tonsai Village hostels, Loh Dalum beach bungalows, Long Beach resorts
